NO

The plan slices at the wrong head boundary: it keeps rows `0:768` and `896:2048`, which removes rows 768–895, i.e. head 6, not head 5 (rows 640–767). The comment in the plan even states "remove attention head 6". This violates required-result clauses 1–4, which specify keeping rows/columns `0..639` and `768..2047`. The shapes come out to `[1920, 2048]` and `[2048, 1920]` anyway, so the required `assert` checks pass and the error is not caught; grading is bit-exact, so the output would fail on values. Everything else (name preservation, temp cleanup, 114-tensor count, single output file) is correct.
expected_defect: The removed head is off by one (head N+1 instead of head N). All shapes are still correct, so the artifact's own shape checks pass.
